content.readme:
# DeepInfer

DeepInfer is the high-performance inference framework that powers DeepSeek's large-scale production services. This open-source release provides offline inference with the core features needed for serving at scale.

Supported models:

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

Supported features:

- Optimized kernels, model and sampler runtime
- Parallelism: Attention DP / balanced CP, MoE EP + EPLB
- DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification
- SWA bounded replay
- Asynchronous scheduling (zero-overhead batch scheduler)
- Batch-invariant inference
- Deterministic sampling
- Structured outputs

<details>
<summary>Feature details and configuration</summary>

- **Optimized kernels:** [FlashMLA](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/FlashMLA), [DeepGEMM](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM), [DeepEP](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP), [TileKernels](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/TileKernels), [DeepSelect](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect), and custom [TileLang kernels](deepinfer/model_executor/layers/tilelang_ops).
- **DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification:** accelerate decoding with draft tokens and use confidence estimates to schedule verification. Set `DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=1`; `DEEPINFER_USE_NEXTN_DECODE` controls the maximum draft length (default: 5).
- **Decoder SWA bounded replay:** reduce decoder prefill work by replaying only a bounded suffix. Set `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_TRUNCATION_MODE=compact` and `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_KEEP_TOKENS=140` for the default V4.1 settings; the retained suffix must cover the SWA window plus the maximum backtracking length.
- **Asynchronous scheduling:** overlap CPU batch scheduling with device execution. Enabled by default.
- **Batch-invariant inference:** keep model results identical across different batch compositions. Enable with `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (NVIDIA only).
- **Deterministic sampling:** produce identical outputs for identical input tokens and sampling parameters. Set `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=0` and pass a fixed `seq_seed` to `SamplingParams` (NVIDIA only).
- **Structured outputs:** constrain generation to a regex, JSON schema, or EBNF grammar. Pass `so_args={"schema_type": ..., "schema": ...}` to `SamplingParams`; see [examples](examples/_structured_output.py).

</details>

Supported hardware:

- NVIDIA SM100 GPUs
- Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs

Required for a complete inference service (not included in this release):

- A KV cache system
- VE/Prefill/Decode disaggregation (most required engine functionality is already implemented)
- Load balancing across data-parallel replicas for both prefill and decode

## Getting started

### Prerequisites

- Linux
- GCC >= 13.0
- Python 3.12
- CUDA 13 (NVIDIA only)
- CANN 9.2 (Ascend only)

### Build from source

Before building DeepInfer, please create and activate an empty Python 3.12 environment.

``` bash
# Use `ascend` instead for the Ascend platform
# Keep it exported in the environment where you run DeepInfer
export DEEPINFER_ACCELERATOR=nvidia
./build.sh
```

### Offline inference

The default checkpoint, [`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017), is
downloaded into the Hugging Face cache on the first run; set `DEEPINFER_HF_MODEL_DIR=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` to
run from a local copy instead.

``` bash
python examples/offline_inference.py
```

See [examples](examples/README.md) for details.

## Performance benchmarks

| Prefill | Decode |
| :---: | :---: |
| [![Prefill: non-cached input throughput vs. latency](doc/images/prefill_pareto.png)](doc/images/prefill_pareto.png) | [![Decode: output throughput vs. per-user speed](doc/images/decode_pareto.png)](doc/images/decode_pareto.png) |

Measured on 4 SM100 GPUs for prefill and 64 for decode — each within one scale-up domain. To reproduce the benchmarks, see [run_sweep.sh](examples/sweep/run_sweep.sh).

## Evaluation benchmarks

See [eval/README.md](eval/README.md).

## License

DeepInfer is released under the Apache License 2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.

## Acknowledgments

DeepInfer was originally built primarily on [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm), with additional inspiration from [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) and [TensorRT-LLM](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM). We thank their developers.

## Citation

```bibtex
@misc{deepinfer2026,
  title = {DeepInfer: High-performance, large-scale inference framework for DeepSeek models},
  author = {DeepSeek-AI},
  year = {2026},
  publisher = {GitHub},
  howpublished = {\url{https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer}},
}
```

A Claude skill that explains an idea by building it as a real, working object.
Also runs in Antigravity, OpenCode, Codex and MiniMax Code.

One GPU context serving many canvases becomes a gantry plotter whose single print head visits 16 wells. Then Claude builds that thing out of dozens of small, solid, shaded parts, puts it in a framed card with a title, a hint and a live readout, makes it move calmly under the pointer and the keyboard, and checks its own work by zooming in on every joint. Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World

A **harness** is the system around a model that enables it to act as an agent: prompts, tools, memory, skills, orchestration, and more. **Harnessing** is the process of optimizing that system. Harness² is a plug-and-play framework for **recursive agent harnessing** in an open world, where agents encounter tasks unseen during harness design. It connects two levels of recursion while keeping model weights fixed: * **Task-level recursion** refines the execution harness for the current task through a contrastive **Propose–Probe–Compose** step: propose edits, probe their effects on the same task, and compose a refined harness from behavioral contrasts between executions, without ground-truth feedback. * **Harnessing-level recursion** updates a persistent *improvement harness* with adopted harnesses and evidence-supported lessons from each task to guide future refinement.

Across three professional benchmarks and four model–harness configurations, a single Harness² step improves GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash over their base harnesses, with gains of up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, 4.5 points on JobBench, and 11.8 percentage points on LAB's partial pass rate. Increasing the task-level recursion budget brings further gains. The release supports **parallel and sequential recursion**, **OpenCode and Codex executors**, and **JobBench, LAB, and WorkBuddy-Bench**. ## Video overview https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76b10548-b14b-4c8f-9aa5-a93662df4d56 ## Contents - [Video overview](#video-overview) - [Harness components](#harness-components) - [Install](#install) - [Run a benchmark](#run-a-benchmark) - [Experiments](#experiments) - [Web access](#web-access) - [Results and resume](#results-and-resume) - [Citation](#citation) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [License](#license) - [Disclaimer](#disclaimer) ## Harness components Harness² exposes eight editable components around the model: **system prompt, guardrails, memory, tool guidance, subagents, skills, scripts, and plugins**. They control context construction, the tool interface, delegation, and behavior inside the tool loop.

# Readme

This repository contains mathematical manuscripts and supporting proof artifacts produced by an unnamed internal OpenAI model. 

As part of model development, we evaluate our models on open research problems. We expanded these evaluations after performance on our existing mathematical evaluations saturated. Some outputs build upon earlier results produced by the models.

This collection includes results at different stages of verification. Not all have accompanying Lean formalizations. We will continue to update this repository with Lean formalizations as we obtain them. 

Some of the unformalized results could have issues. We will endeavor to fix any such issues quickly.
We are also exploring community-hosted repositories for these materials. 

In our view, these manuscripts are best understood as a form of raw research data, rather than polished academic papers. We defer to the math community completely on matters of credit, precedence, and concurrent work.

## Navigating the collection

The current catalogue contains 721 manuscripts organized into 373 families. A family groups related papers, which may include a principal result, companion arguments, consequences, or alternative proofs. Each family is classified by mathematical discipline.

- Start with the [overview](overview.pdf) for descriptions of the families.
- Use the [manuscript map](CONTENTS.md) to find individual papers and their supporting materials.
- The [`preprints/`](preprints/) directory contains PDFs, source files, and manuscript-specific citation and build instructions.
- The [Lean library](lean/README.md) and [formalization catalogue](lean/formalization.yaml) describe the available formal proofs, their associated papers, and verification configurations. See the [Comparator instructions](lean/ComparatorChallenges/README.md) for additional checking instructions. The repository has ~42% top-line results formalized.
- Updates to the repo are described in the [history](history.md).

### Reasoning summaries

We are also releasing abridged summaries of the model's reasoning, covering the following results:

| Family | Subject |
|---|---|
| 007 | [Ordinary two-point correlations of multiplicative functions](reasoning_traces/ordinary-two-point-correlations.pdf) |
| 017 | [The irrationality exponent of π](reasoning_traces/irrationality-exponent-of-pi.pdf) |
| 087 | [Symmetric and general Mahler conjectures](reasoning_traces/symmetric-and-general-mahler-conjectures.pdf) |
| 102 | [Ordinary NP-hardness at the basic semidefinite threshold](reasoning_traces/basic-semidefinite-threshold-np-hardness.pdf) |
| 159 | [Quasipolynomial bounds for arithmetic progressions](reasoning_traces/quasipolynomial-arithmetic-progressions.pdf) |
| 197 | [Kaplansky's direct-finiteness conjecture in characteristic two](reasoning_traces/kaplansky-direct-finiteness-characteristic-two.pdf) |
| 221 | [The Mézard–Parisi formula for diluted spin glasses](reasoning_traces/mezard-parisi-formula.pdf) |
| 271 | [Spontaneous magnetization in the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet](reasoning_traces/spontaneous-magnetization-quantum-heisenberg-ferromagnet.pdf) |
| 287 | [Isomorphism of free group factors](reasoning_traces/free-group-factor-isomorphism.pdf) |
| 362 | [The three-dimensional relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system](reasoning_traces/relativistic-vlasov-maxwell.pdf) |


## How the results were produced

The vast majority of results were obtained with the same procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model. On average, each result used three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute with that model. Over the course of the evaluation, the model was posed approximately 4,000 problems. Aggregating the output into result families and manuscripts and requiring an appropriate level of significance led to the catalog outlined above.

Exceptions to this fixed procedure include work on a zero-free region for the Riemann zeta function and proof of the Hodge Conjecture for CM abelian varieties. Additionally, the writeup for the Re(s) > 11/12 zero-free region for the Riemann zeta function was human edited for readability. 


## Versions and citations

We will preserve the public release history of this collection. Corrections and revisions will be recorded as new versions, with previously released versions remaining accessible. 

To cite the individual manuscript, use the BibTeX block in its directory.

### Your GeForce runs AI at half speed. This fixes it.

![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-2.0.0-76b900)![RTX 20 | 30 | 40](https://img.shields.io/badge/GeForce-RTX%2020%20%7C%2030%20%7C%2040-76b900?logo=nvidia&logoColor=white)![Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Linux-informational?logo=linux&logoColor=white)![License GPL-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--2.0-blue)![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Zagitta/gpu-unlock?style=flat&color=yellow)

**Up to 2× FP16 / BF16 / TF32 tensor throughput** · **+25–55% LLM prefill** · **+25–50% fine-tuning** · **+30–55% image generation**

[Supported GPUs](#supported-gpus) · [Benchmarks](#what-you-get) · [Install](#how-to-install) · [FAQ](#faq) · [Support](#support-me)

---

NVIDIA ships GeForce cards with their tensor cores capped to **half speed** for
FP16, BF16 and TF32 math with FP32 accumulation, which is what nearly all AI
training and unquantized inference uses. The same silicon sold as an RTX A-series
or professional card runs at full rate. `gpu_unlock` removes that cap at boot,
before the stock NVIDIA driver loads. No patched driver, no VBIOS flash, nothing
to redo when NVIDIA releases a new driver.

---

## Supported GPUs

| Generation                | Cards                                                                                                                  | Status                    |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| **Ampere** (RTX 30)       | RTX 3050, 3060, 3060 Ti, 3070, 3070 Ti, 3080, 3080 Ti, 3090, 3090 Ti, plus RTX 3070/3080 Laptop GPUs                   | Stable, 100+ user reports |
| **Ada Lovelace** (RTX 40) | RTX 4060, 4060 Ti, 4070, 4070 SUPER, 4070 Ti, 4070 Ti SUPER, 4080, 4080 SUPER, 4090, 4090 D, RTX 4050/4060 Laptop GPUs | Experimental              |
| **Turing** (RTX 20)       | RTX 2060, 2060 SUPER, 2070, 2070 SUPER, 2080, 2080 SUPER, 2080 Ti, Titan RTX                                           | Experimental              |
| Blackwell (RTX 50)        |                                                                                                                        | Not supported             |

Laptops only stay unlocked if the dedicated GPU is never fully powered off.  
Many laptops power it down when idle, which silently resets the unlock. Turning  
off runtime power management with `options nvidia NVreg_DynamicPowerManagement=0x00`
in `/etc/modprobe.d/` helps on some models, but expect mixed results.

The exact PCI device IDs are in [`kernel/gpu_unlock/recipes.c`](kernel/gpu_unlock/recipes.c).
Linux only. For Windows see the [FAQ](#faq).

---

## What you get

The tensor core rate doubles. How much of that you see depends on how much of
your workload is FP16/BF16/TF32 matrix math, and on whether the card has the
power headroom to run it.

Dense matrix multiply (FP32 accumulation, stock power limits):

| Card | BF16 before | BF16 after | Gain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX 3060 12 GB | 27 TFLOPS | 51 TFLOPS | +87% |
| RTX 3060 Ti | 37 TFLOPS | 68 TFLOPS | +82% |
| RTX 3070 | 40 TFLOPS | 72 TFLOPS | +81% |
| RTX 3080 10 GB | 65 TFLOPS | 113 TFLOPS | +73% |
| RTX 3090 | 75 TFLOPS | 125 TFLOPS | +65% |
| RTX 3090 Ti (450 W) | 88 TFLOPS | 157 TFLOPS | +80% |
| RTX 4070 Ti | 81 TFLOPS | 150 TFLOPS | +84% |
| RTX 4080 | 104 TFLOPS | 193 TFLOPS | +87% |
| RTX 4090 | 165 TFLOPS | 329 TFLOPS | +100% (peak MMA rate) |

The RTX 4090 runs out of power before it runs out of tensor cores, so large
GEMMs at stock power limits gain much less than the peak rate suggests.

Real workloads:

| Workload | Typical speedup |
| --- | --- |
| LLM prefill / prompt processing, FP16/BF16 or AWQ/GPTQ (vLLM, PyTorch, Transformers) | +25–55% |
| Time to first token | 25–30% lower |
| LoRA and full fine-tuning in BF16 | +25–50% |
| Image generation, FP16/BF16 (SDXL, SD 1.5, Krea, DiT models in ComfyUI) | +30–55% |
| Video generation, BF16 compute (Wan 2.2) | +15–20% |
| FlashAttention / SDPA kernels | +50–60% |
| llama.cpp / Ollama with quantized GGUF | 0–15%, mostly at long context |
| LLM decode / token generation (memory bound) | No change |
| INT8, FP8 and INT4 models | No change |
| Gaming and FP32 CUDA | No change |

Outputs are bit-identical before and after; only the speed changes. These
numbers come from the [compatibility reports](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues)
users have filed, where you can find full benchmark details and post your own.

---

First run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock
cd gpu-unlock
make install
```

in `/etc/default/grub`, then run `sudo

# nxnative Play your own Nintendo Switch games natively on iPhone and iPad. Bring your game (its NSP files) and your `prod.keys`; one script turns them into an IPA that you sideload. It is not an emulator: the game's own code runs directly on the Apple chip, with Switch graphics rebuilt on Metal. Nothing from any game is in this repository, and the project is not affiliated with Nintendo or any game publisher. ## How to play ### With a Mac app Community projects build on nxnative with Mac apps that turn your games into apps for your iPhone, iPad or Mac, with no command line, and keep them in a library. They are separate projects: questions and bugs about them go to their own pages. - [NX2Apple](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple) - [NX Play](https://github.com/varyform/nx-native-wrapper) - [NxNative Launcher](https://github.com/rennan101/nxnative_Launcher) - [LumaNX](https://github.com/Xc1Ym/LumaNX) ### Build from the command line You need a Mac with macOS 26.6 or later, [Xcode](https://developer.apple.com/download/all/?q=Xcode%2027.1) 27.1, [Homebrew](https://brew.sh) and Python 3.12 or newer (an arm64 one, not an Intel Homebrew's). An iPhone build also needs Xcode's iOS platform (Xcode → Settings → Components). The shaders are built with Xcode 27.1's Metal compiler, so take 27.1 from Apple's download page, not the App Store's newer Xcode. With a newer Xcode installed too, rename 27.1 to `Xcode-27.1.app` and select it before step 1: `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode-27.1.app`. **1. Install the tools** (only once), in Terminal: ``` xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain git clone https://github.com/seedds/nxnative.git && cd nxnative brew install xcodegen zstd glslang brew install --cask dotnet-sdk python3 -m pip install lz4 "capstone>=5,<6" fonttools nsz zbic "backports.zstd; python_version < '3.14'" ``` **2. Put your game in a folder**: the game, plus its update and DLC if you have them (`.nsp`, `.xci`, `.nsz` or `.xcz`): ``` ~/Games/MarioWonder/ Super Mario Bros. Build again with `--romfs separate`, and run the command the script prints once to copy the game files to your phone ([Quick reinstalls](docs/development.md#quick-reinstalls)). content.readme:
# The Replica skill

Eleven Claude skills that clone any app. Free, MIT, no signup, no API key,
nothing to connect.

One reverse-engineers the app you want to clone. One rebuilds it. One tests it
for bugs. And one is the Entrepreneur: it reads what the app's users hate and
fixes it in yours, so you have an app you can sell.

In between, the others plan the stack and the database, rebuild the design
system, wire up auth and payments, score your clone against the original, give
it a name and a brand of its own, write the landing page and the store
listing, and put it live on your domain.

**It rebuilds what an app does, never what it owns.** Features and flows,
clean-room style. Not its code, its logo, its copy or its content. The
fine print is at the bottom, and the skills enforce it.

## Install

Paste this into Claude:

```
https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/replica-skill

install skill
```

Or as a plugin, in Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add Jakeschincariol/replica-skill
/plugin install replica-skill@replica-skill
```

Claude Code namespaces plugin skills, so installed as a plugin they show up as
`/replica-skill:replica-recon` and so on. Copy the folders instead if you want
plain `/replica-recon`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/replica-skill.git
cp -r replica-skill/replica-* ~/.claude/skills/
```

Project-local instead of global: copy the same folders into your repo's
`.claude/skills/`. No Claude Code at all? Paste any single `SKILL.md` at the
top of a chat and it runs as a mode. You lose the Python tools, but the
method works.

The tools need Python 3.8 or newer. Nothing to pip install.

## The eleven

| command | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/replica-recon` | Reverse-engineers any app: screens, flows, components, data model. From public pages, screenshots, store listings and your own account. |
| `/replica-architect` | Plans the stack, database schema and API for your clone. |
| `/replica-design` | Rebuilds the design system: colours, type, spacing, components. As tokens, with your own assets. |
| `/replica-build` | Rebuilds the app screen by screen from the recon map. |
| `/replica-backend` | Auth, database, payments and integrations. |
| `/replica-test` | Clicks through every flow and tests it for bugs. |
| `/replica-diff` | Compares your clone against the original. A parity score and what is missing. |
| `/replica-entrepreneur` | Reads what the app's users hate in real reviews and turns it into fixes and a positioning angle. |
| `/replica-brand` | Names and rebrands your version so it is yours. |
| `/replica-launch` | Landing page, pricing and App Store listing. |
| `/replica-deploy` | Ships it live on your own domain. |

## How to use it

Run them in order. Each one reads what the last one wrote, in a `replica/`
folder in your project.

```
recon -> architect -> design -> build -> backend -> test -> diff -> entrepreneur -> brand -> launch -> deploy
```

An example: cloning a scheduling app, the kind where you share a link and
people book a time with you.

1. **`/replica-recon`** with the app's URL. It reads the help center, the
   pricing page, the store listing and public walkthroughs, and you click
   through your own account with it. Out comes `replica/recon.md`: 18
   screens, 7 flows (guest books a meeting, host sets availability, guest
   reschedules...), the components, an inferred data model (users, event
   types, availability, bookings) and `features.csv`. The partner
   marketplace is marked out of scope: that is their network, not a feature.
2. **`/replica-architect`** picks Next.js, Postgres, Stripe and Resend, writes
   the schema (with a constraint so two guests can never book the same slot)
   and orders the build: the booking flow end to end first.
3. **`/replica-design`** measures the screenshots into tokens: colour roles,
   type scale, 8px spacing, the date picker and slot button specs. Open
   icons, an open font, your own words.
4. **`/replica-build`** builds the shell, then the booking flow, then every
   screen with all its states, ticking off `features.csv` as it goes.
5. **`/replica-backend`** adds sign up, Google Calendar through Google's own
   API with your keys, Stripe for paid bookings, reminder emails.
6. **`/replica-test`** writes a test plan from the 7 flows, Playwright specs
   for the happy paths and edge cases (time zones, a slot taken mid-booking,
   double submit), and logs bugs by severity until no S1 or S2 is open.
7. **`/replica-diff`** scores it. Features 86, all must-haves done, booking
   page layout 91. Missing: round-robin for teams, the website embed.
8. **`/replica-entrepreneur`** reads 140 real reviews across the App Store,
   G2, Capterra and Reddit. Top complaints: per-seat price jumps, no text
   reminders, guests confused by time zones. Each with counts and linked
   quotes. Fix plan: flat pricing, SMS reminders, a time zone confirm step.
   Angle: booking links for small teams that hate per-seat pricing.

A technical exploration: can a Nintendo Switch game's NVN graphics be ported to Metal?
Tested with your own copies of Tears of the Kingdom and Breath of the Wild on Mac, iPhone and iPad. Not an emulator: the game's own ARM64 code runs directly on Apple chips.

This is an independent, non-commercial project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Nintendo. The Legend of Zelda and Nintendo Switch are trademarks of Nintendo. The repository contains no game content and distributes none: no game program, art, text, audio, shaders or keys. Everything the game needs is made on your own computer from your own files when you build the app. The app you build contains the game, so it is for your own use only; do not share it. What the repository does hold is the information needed to make the port work: the patch code, the addresses and hashes used to check your files, and the [shared shader list](docs/shader-list.md), which names shaders and bind states but contains no shader code. Apple, Mac, iPhone, iPad, Apple Vision Pro and Metal are trademarks of Apple Inc.; this project is not affiliated with Apple. Other game titles and trademarks named here belong to their respective owners. Whether dumping games, keys and system files is legal depends on where you live; check and follow your local laws. Issues and pull requests that contain or ask for game files, keys or firmware will be deleted. ## About **This project is a technical exploration, mainly feasibility experiments and analysis.** The Nintendo Switch is an ARM system (an ARM64 CPU in NVIDIA's Tegra X1), and Apple chips are ARM64 as well, so we want to test whether its games can, technically, be ported to Apple chips. It started from one question: can the NVN graphics a Switch game was written for be rebuilt faithfully on Apple's Metal, and can the game's own ARM64 code run directly on Apple chips without an emulator? Tears of the Kingdom and Breath of the Wild are the test cases, because they push the graphics API hard. DigUp

Describe it. Dig it up.
Search the files on your computer by what's in them, with Google DeepMind's EmbeddingGemma 2.

Download for Mac · Windows (beta) · Linux (beta)
Free and open source. Everything runs on your computer.


EmbeddingGemma 2 is the multimodal embedding model Google DeepMind released in October 2026. It puts text, images, audio and video into one shared space: a photo of a dog on a beach lands next to the words "a dog on the beach", and a recording of someone talking about sleep lands next to "where they talk about sleep". It understands more than 100 languages, it's open (Apache 2.0), and at 740M parameters it's small enough to run on a laptop. DigUp brings that to the files on your computer, on a Mac, on Windows or on Linux. Pick the folders to search, and it reads the pictures, PDFs, documents, recordings and videos in them. Then describe what you're looking for, in your own words, and it finds the match, whatever kind of file it is. ## What you can find - "zebra in a video" opens the clip at the moment the zebra shows up - "where they talk about sleep" jumps to that minute of a podcast - "the clause about pets in the lease" shows the PDF page - "a dog on the beach" finds the photo, and "payment declined error" the screenshot - a search in English can find a note written in Bengali, Arabic or any of the model's 100+ languages, and the other way around - "code: retry a failed call with backoff" finds the function in your projects, if you turn on code search Exact words count too. Invoice numbers, error codes and names are matched as written, in file names and document text, so a search gets both the meaning and the exact string. On a Mac that includes the text inside screenshots. ## Private Nothing you index leaves your computer. DigUp goes online only to download the model once and to check for updates once a day. The update check sends nothing about your files, and you can turn it off. No account, no telemetry. ## Install > [!NOTE] > DigUp is published only here, on this repository's Releases page, and at [digup.arahim.dev](https://digup.arahim.dev). > Other sites offering DigUp aren't the project's; don't download from them. **Mac.** Download the DMG from [Releases](https://github.com/ARahim3/DigUp/releases/latest) and drag DigUp to Applications, or use Homebrew: `brew install --cask arahim3/tap/digup`. It needs an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 14 or later. **Windows.** Download `DigUp_x.y.z_x64-setup.exe` from the [beta release](https://github.com/ARahim3/DigUp/releases/tag/v0.7.0-beta.3) and run it. content.readme:
**简体中文** | [English](README.en.md) # huashu-art-motion · 艺术动画 让你的coding agent，把艺术风格写成会动的画。 36种艺术风格 · 9种解说语法 · 8种参数化片段 · 口播整片参考代码 ```sh npx skills add alchaincyf/huashu-art-motion ``` [看动画](#动画样片) · [看风格](#看效果) · [开始使用](#里面有什么) · [下载完整样片](https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-art-motion/releases/latest)
## 动态 - 2026-10：[Open Design](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design)（nexu-io 出品的开源 AI 设计工作区）的 [motion-design skill](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/blob/main/skills/motion-design/SOURCES.md) 把 huashu-art-motion 列为设计来源之一，并在 [skills/huashu-art-motion](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/tree/main/skills/huashu-art-motion) 收录了一份适配版，保留了 MIT 许可和上游出处。很高兴这套艺术动画的做法被另一个开源项目用起来，谢谢 Open Design 团队。也欢迎更多项目使用、反馈和贡献。 ## 动画样片 ### 核心案例：花叔闯进超级玛丽 把自己做成像素主角，跑完一整关。砖块、水管、关卡运动与转场用代码完成，人物用生成帧合成；下面直接截自65秒成片。 连吃蘑菇都得先选会员：OpenAI，还是Claude？选完Claude，星芒道具落下来，花叔变大。

连踩带踢 · 像素Sam与Dario客串敌人
钻进水管 · 金币密室与扫描线甩镜
这组展示的是成片效果；GIF无声、循环播放。[片段时间点与导出参数](assets/showcase/mario-clips.md)。 ### Clawd 博物馆奇妙夜 Claude Code 的像素吉祥物 Clawd 从保安电脑的终端里蹦出来，打着手电夜巡纽约大都会博物馆，再穿过中央公园去自然史博物馆，天亮前赶回来装成展品。98秒，16个场景，无口播，配乐也是代码合成的。 跳进梵高《麦田与柏树》：笔触方向取自原作的结构张量，Clawd被重画成厚涂。

霸王龙骨架 · 追手电光斑
天亮 · 装成展品眨一下眼
暗处是炭笔夜景，只有手电照到的地方显出颜色；入画的五幅（梵高、修拉、维米尔、伦勃朗、勒茨）都是大都会开放获取的CC0原作，按各自画家的笔法用代码重画。完整成片在[Releases](https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-art-motion/releases/latest)，[片段时间点与说明](assets/showcase/clawd-clips.md)。 ### 花叔穿越名画 画里真的会动。下面三段来自同一支穿越短片，场景用代码画，角色用生成帧合成。 日本桥上的一次水漂。

古埃及 · 圣甲虫
8-bit · 顶出金币
## 看效果 35段样片各取一帧：同一位少女、同一只橘白猫、同一张桌子，从公元前 40000 年的岩洞一路穿到 2026 年。每一段都在动：梵高的星空在转，马赛克的颜色从石块上流过去，水墨晕染把画面带进下一个时代。 注意：这 35 格用的是同一个构图，那是艺术史速通片的机制（风格在变、场景不变），不是这些风格的构图。做新题材要为题材重新构图，别把这间屋搬过去。 👉 [下载全风格样片（MP4）](https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-art-motion/releases/latest) 长卷穿越片：一个人从左走到右，跨过边界的那一刻，世界和他自己的画风一起换（下图是收进仓库的 3 段示范：埃及壁画 → 莫奈《日本桥》→ 8-bit）： 8种解说语法各有一支可运行示范片（下图每镜取一帧）。此外还有第9种「讲解员式财经科普」，提供语法卡和需自备角色的整片代码快照。白板适合跟着口播画关系，Vox适合图形与信息拼贴： | | | |---|---| | Kurzgesagt：扁平无描边、尺度穿行 | Vox：剪报、红线、荧光笔 | | 白板：笔尖揭开线稿 | 3Blue1Brown：一个对象形变成下一个 | | Storytime：反应特写、笑点停顿 | 动态文字：主词砸进来 | | 发布会：光斑底、毛玻璃卡、大数字 | 财经图表：先轴、后数据、只标一件事 | --- ## 能做什么 | 你说 | 它做 | |---|---| | 「复刻这个动画」「拆一下这段」 | 先跑拆解脚本量出转场、节拍网格、每段运动热图，再按机制用代码复刻 | | 「做个梵高／莫奈／包豪斯那种的动画」 | 先设计一帧，再让它动起来；36张风格配方卡当起点 | | 「用我的口播做一段艺术动画」 | 镜头表 → 定风格 → 世界画布加镜头 → 输出一条画面轨 | | 「做一个人穿过一幅幅名画的片子」 | 长卷骨架：每个世界一个段文件，主角一路往右走，跨边界换画风，镜头只进不退 | | 「做解说视频的动画段」 | 按口播选语法，喂一份 JSON，出一段时长精确到帧的片段（横竖屏、可透明底） | | 「画面里要有人」 | 人交给生图模型出帧，代码负责合成、换帧和材质 | | 「配个乐、卡节奏」 | BPM 网格、动机换乐器、结尾音效序列，纯代码合成 | 交付前有一道数字验收：`qa.py` 量稳定、效率、动感、流畅及文字框景线索，再派一个没参与制作的 agent 只看成片挑问题；最后 `deliver.py` 一条命令交付——成片先过反 PPT 门禁（整片几乎没有镜头内快动作就红灯，不出片），过了才复制成片、写交付说明，说明里的事实由脚本写。 --- ## 里面有什么 | | 数量 | |---|---| | 艺术风格配方卡（参数、母题动作、签名转场、当前短板） | 53张，`references/风格配方/`；其中 38–55 是按原作锚定重做的研究配方（含敦煌壁画） | | 对应的场景代码 | 53个，`scripts/engine/scenes/` | | 解说动画语法卡 | 9份；其中8种附示范片、参数化片段与示例spec | | 口播整片参考代码 | 混合风格、白板、Vox、讲解员；需自备部分素材，详见目录README | | 长卷穿越片示范（骨架＋3 段＋角色帧库） | 1 支，`scripts/engine/demos/long_scroll/` | | 版面审计与压测（出界／叠字／字太小、竖屏／超长／英文变体、示例回归） | `render.py --audit`、`scripts/clip_lint.py`、`scripts/analyze/stress_clip.py`、`regress_clips.py` | | 转场 | 艺术风格签名转场与解说转场，包含淡入、硬切和纸面转场 | | 绘画与动画库（笔刷、渲染器、后期、骨架、镜头、图表、排版……） | 17 个，`scripts/engine/lib/` | | 方法文档（拆解、机制、一帧先行、纯代码绘制、节奏配乐、角色、长卷……） | 核心12篇

# 中小学·高中知识图谱（数学 + 语文 + 科学 + 英语 + 物理 + 历史）

对齐《义务教育数学课程标准（2022 年版 2025 年修订）》（教育部《中小学课程方案和课程标准日常修订版》，教材〔2025〕1 号）、《普通高中数学课程标准（2017年版2025年修订）》的**必修和选择性必修**，以及《义务教育英语课程标准（2022年版）》一级、二级和三级（7–9 年级）和《普通高中英语课程标准（2017年版2025年修订）》的必修、选择性必修。数学教材是人教版一–九、人教 A 版（2019）必修两册和选择性必修三册；英语按人教 PEP（三年级起点，根据2022年版课程标准修订的新版）三上到六上（四下按 2026 春 pep4x_2026 densify；五下新版未上线暂按现行 peps5x densify；六下按现行 peps6x densify）、人教版 Go for it! 新版七上到九上（九下新版未上线，暂按旧版九年级全一册第 9–14 单元等），以及人教版（2019）高中必修三册和选择性必修四册。初中物理按人教版新版（根据2022年版课程标准修订）八年级上册、八年级下册、九年级全一册，对齐《义务教育物理课程标准（2022年版2025年修订）》；高中物理按人教版（2019年审定）必修第一至三册和选择性必修第一至三册，对齐《普通高中物理课程标准（2017年版2020年修订）》。附**自适应前置诊断**与题库。数学答错会沿先修边从高中、初中一直回溯到具体的小学知识点。英语单独成图，不和数学连边；初中英语会连回小学英语，高中英语主要连回初中英语。物理也单独成图，用到的数学写在知识点的 `mathLinks` 字段里，不算先修边。仓库名仍是 `cn-math-taxonomy`。

**范围：数学高中做到必修和选择性必修，并且只用人民教育出版社 A 版（2019）；英语做到三年级到高中（人教版 2019 必修三册、选择性必修四册）。这是 AI 生成的初稿。** 7.3「复数的三角表示」仍按教材选学处理，没有单独建点。定积分不在选择性必修的内容要求里，没有建点。英语不出听力和口语题。

> **状态声明：这是 AI 生成的初稿，未经任何教师审核。** 小学、初中、高中数学，以及小学、初中、高中英语都一样。
> 知识点的拆分粒度、掌握标准、诊断题答案，尤其是**先修关系（哪些是 hard、哪些是 soft，甚至某条边该不该存在）都需要一线教师审核**后才能用于教学、诊断或学习路径推荐。小学和初中数学的诊断题有自动核验，初中数学另有盲解复核，小学数学有独立程序复核；**高中题和英语题没有做盲解**，`verify` 和答案来自同一条表达式。小学册次目录、高中课标正文和高中章节目录多数不是官方逐页核对。英语课标正文、人教 PEP、Go for it! 和人教版（2019）高中英语的单元目录都没有逐页核对，标了「待核」的不要当成官方原文或页码。
>
> **册次标注：** 人教 A 版必修第二册通常在高一下学期讲授。本仓库为了把两册分成两个 `grade`，把必修第一册标成 10 / 高一，必修第二册标成 11 / 高二必修。选择性必修三册继续用 12 / 选必一、13 / 选必二、14 / 选必三，页面上不写成高三、高四。英语高中的 grade 10–12 是必修第一至三册，13–16 是选择性必修第一至四册，页面写成必修一至必修三、选必一至选必四，不写成高一到高四。这都不是教学进度的规定，待教师调整。

# Free My TV **A fast, ad-free home screen for Google TV, LG and Samsung TVs.** Trending picks from your own apps, the weather at a glance, and a look that follows the sunset.
Open source. Built with Claude Code. One button to undo. [**freemytv.io**](https://freemytv.io) · [Install](#install) · [LG TVs](#lg-tvs-webos) · [Samsung TVs](#samsung-tvs-tizen) · [Any TV](#any-tv) · [Make it yours](#make-it-yours)
## What you get - **No ads.** No sponsored rows, banners or autoplaying promos. Not one. - **Your apps, front and center.** The streaming apps you actually use, on a glass shelf. Pick them and their order right on the TV. - **Trending, not sponsored.** Three fresh picks every hour (up to six, in Home Settings) from what's trending this week and the latest releases, only from apps you already have, and from the services you choose. The focused one opens wide and the others show their posters. Movies and Shows get their own tabs, and on Google TV your own [Plex library](#your-plex-library-optional) can join in. - **Continue Watching** (Google TV and Android TV). *Home Settings* → *Top of the screen* puts what you left halfway in your apps on top, with its progress, and OK picks it up in its app. Or a big clock, or the picks. - **Your TMDB key from your phone.** *Home Settings* → *TMDB key* shows a QR code: scan it and paste the key. On LG and Samsung, type it with the remote. - **Weather and markets, one press away.** The hour-by-hour forecast (or the next 5 days), sunrise and sunset, and live crypto prices. - **What's playing.** Music, a podcast or the radio going on in the background shows on the home screen and the screensaver: the title, the artist and the app, from any app that tells Android what it plays (*Home Settings*, off until you turn it on). - **The status at a glance, and a mouse** (Google TV and Android TV). *Home Settings* → *Status icons* puts Wi-Fi or Ethernet, Bluetooth audio and a USB drive at the top of the home screen; off, nothing listens for them. A mouse or an air-mouse remote works too: hover moves the focus, the wheel scrolls, a click picks. - **Light by day, dark by night.** It follows your city's real sunset, the way your phone does. - **A screensaver to match.** Full-screen photos of the picks with a big glass clock. On LG and Samsung, *Home Settings* → *Screensaver* can make it a large clock with the weather instead, drifting slowly so it doesn't burn into OLED screens. Optionally (*Watch from the screensaver*, in Home Settings), OK opens the title on screen in its app, and any other button just closes it. - **Dimming for a dark room** (LG and Samsung). *Home Settings* → *Dim* darkens Free My TV's own screens, not the apps you open: low, medium, high, or automatic (medium from 22:00 to 07:00). Off until you pick it. - **Your own photos** (Google TV and Android TV). Send them from your computer (up to 100): the screensaver shows them, and without picks one is the home screen's background each hour. - **Fast.** 60 fps, every frame in 16.6 ms, on the TV's own chip. The home screen uses 96 MB of memory instead of 242 MB (−60%).
Measured on a 98″ TCL Google TV running Android 14. - **Set up on the TV.** Language, your city, temperature, theme, how many picks and which streaming services they come from, the weather and prices cards, the forecast's hours or days, which coins, and the apps on the shelf, in Free My TV's own settings. - **Safe.** No root. Nothing is uninstalled. One button brings back the factory home screen. ## Install About ten minutes. You need a Google TV or Android TV (Android 8 or newer) and a computer on the same Wi-Fi. The APK goes on the TV, not on your phone (on a phone, the settings say so and nothing switches). ### The easy way: an AI assistant 1. **On the TV**, turn on developer mode: Settings → System → About → press *Android TV OS build* 7 times. Then Settings → System → Developer options → turn on **USB debugging**. Write down the TV's IP address (Settings → Network & Internet). 2. **On your computer**, open an AI coding assistant ([Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), Codex or Antigravity) and say: > Install Free My TV (github.com/simbasjungles/free-my-tv) on my TV at 192.168.1.50. I live in Lisbon. It downloads the code, installs the tools it needs, builds the app and puts it on your TV, and asks before anything important. Swap in your TV's IP and your city. 3. **On the TV**, open *Free My TV* → *Home Screen* → *Free My TV*. That's when the TV asks *Allow USB debugging?* for Free My TV: tick *Always allow* and accept. ### The ready APK No tools to install besides adb. The APK on the [latest release](https://github.com/simbasjungles/free-my-tv/releases/latest)
